newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW Govt calls for Australia tax reform summit.
newsitem.headline: NSW Govt calls for Australia tax reform summit.

text.p: New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan on Wednesday called on his fellow state governments and the federal government to meet within four to five years to reform the nation's tax system.
Egan said the various government's should follow the model they used to successfully decide on joint nationwide microeconomic reforms to deregulate gas and electricity markets around Australia.
"Tax reform and Commonwealth/State Financial relations do have to go on the reform agenda," Egan told a breakfast function presenting the state budget for 1997/98 (July-June).

The budget included various new small taxes, including a 10 percent bed tax on Sydney hotels, that some commentators have described as a way of taxing Australia's services sector in the absence a nationwide Goods and Services Tax (GST).
Current sales taxes are concentrated on the traded goods sector, leaving sales from service industries like tourism and telecommunications untaxed.
The conservative Liberal/National government has ruled out bringing in a GST in its current term of office which ends in 1999, but has said the issue should be debated.
The government is widely expected to consider a GST in its second term if it wins the 1999 election.
"COAG (Council of Australian Governments) is the model that we should be following," Egan said.
"We should use that model to overhaul our tax arrangements in Australia," he said.
